w: Opened in 1978 to mark Indonesian independence, Istiqlal - Arabic for 'independence' - is Southeast Asia's largest mosque and ranks ninth-largest worldwide by capacity. It stands beside Merdeka Square within sight of the Catholic Jakarta Cathedral and the Reformed Immanuel Church: three faiths, one square.
s: Southeast Asia's largest mosque, named for freedom
_facts: Largest mosque in Southeast Asia, ninth largest in the world by worshipper capacity
Built to commemorate Indonesian independence, named 'Istiqlal' (independence)
Opened to the public 22 February 1978
Positioned next to Merdeka Square, near Jakarta Cathedral (Catholic) and Immanuel Church (Reformed)

w: Built as the residence of the Dutch East Indies' governors-general and known then as Paleis te Koningsplein, this palace was renamed Merdeka - freedom - in 1949 and became the Indonesian president's official residence. It anchors a 6.8-hectare presidential compound still at the centre of executive power today.
s: A Dutch governor-general's house, renamed for freedom
_facts: Located on north side of Merdeka Square, Central Jakarta
One of seven presidential palaces of Indonesia
Residence for Dutch East Indies governors-general during colonial era, known as Paleis te Koningsplein
Renamed Merdeka Palace in 1949 ('merdeka' = freedom/independence)
Part of 6.8ha Jakarta Presidential Palace Complex, centre of executive authority

w: Nicknamed the Elephant Museum for the statue guarding its forecourt, this collection spans prehistory to modern Indonesia across 141,000 objects - Hindu-Buddhist stone statues from Java and Sumatra, Asian ceramics, and two centuries of accumulated heritage. A 2023 fire closed rooms for renovation until late 2024.
s: The Elephant Museum, minus the elephant out front
_facts: Located on Jalan Medan Merdeka Barat, west side of Merdeka Square
Popularly called Museum Gajah (Elephant Museum) after elephant statue in forecourt
Preserves about 141,000 objects across archaeology, numismatics, ceramics, ethnography, history, geography
Comprehensive Hindu-Buddhist stone statue collections from Java and Sumatra
Fire on 16 Sept 2023 closed some rooms; reopened after renovation October 2024

w: Jakarta's whole story starts here - Sunda Kelapa was the Sunda Kingdom's main port before the city grew up around it. Now reduced to a minor harbour on the Ciliwung estuary, it still runs a working fleet of pinisi, twin-masted wooden schooners hauling inter-island freight the old-fashioned way.
s: Jakarta's original harbour, still under sail
_facts: Old port of Jakarta at the estuary of the Ciliwung River
Original name means 'Coconut of Sunda'; was main port of the Sunda Kingdom
Located in Penjaringan District, North Jakarta
Today accommodates pinisi, traditional two-masted wooden sailing ships for inter-island freight
Operated by state-owned Indonesia Port Corporation (Pelindo)

w: Built in 1710 as Batavia's Stadhuis, or city hall, and said to be modelled on Amsterdam's Dam Palace, this Kota Tua building has run as a museum since 1974. Its rooms track the city from prehistory through Jayakarta's 1527 founding to Dutch colonisation and 1945 independence - one address, four centuries.
s: Batavia's old city hall, modelled on a Dutch palace
_facts: Also known as Fatahillah Museum or Batavia Museum, in Kota Tua (Old Town)
Building built 1710 as the Stadhuis (city hall) of Batavia
Opened as museum 1974
Displays objects from prehistory, founding of Jayakarta 1527, Dutch colonisation through 1945 independence
Believed modelled after Dam Palace, Amsterdam

w: Sculptor Edhi Sunarso completed this welcome monument in 1962, and it's stood at the centre of the Hotel Indonesia roundabout ever since, greeting whoever circles it. One of the city's oldest surviving landmarks, doing traffic-island duty as a piece of civic history.
s: The bronze couple welcoming traffic since 1962
_facts: Also known as Monumen Bundaran HI
Located at centre of Bundaran Hotel Indonesia roundabout, Central Jakarta
Completed 1962 by sculptor Edhi Sunarso
One of the historic landmarks of Jakarta

w: Opened in 1864 and relocated to its current 140-hectare South Jakarta site, Ragunan is Indonesia's oldest zoo and the city's largest park, running an aviary and primate centre for over 2,000 animals. Crocodiles, orangutans and Sumatran tigers get ample room in a lush layout - rare, in a menagerie this old.
s: Indonesia's oldest zoo, 162 years and counting
_facts: Located in Pasar Minggu, South Jakarta; 140-hectare area, largest park in Jakarta
Aviary and primate centre; over 450 staff, 2,288 animals total
Endangered species include crocodile, chimpanzee, gorilla, orangutan, tapir, anoa, Sumatran tiger, babirusa
Originally opened 1864 (later redeveloped into Ismail Marzuki Park site); oldest zoo in Indonesia at 162 years old

w: One of the first five-star hotels built anywhere in Southeast Asia, Hotel Indonesia became so bound up with the nation's post-independence pride that the roundabout out front simply took its name - Bundaran HI. Now run as the Kempinski, it still anchors the intersection it created.
s: Southeast Asia's first five-star, still standing
_facts: Hotel Indonesia Kempinski Jakarta, one of oldest and best-known hotels in Jakarta
One of the first 5-star hotels in Southeast Asia
Major landmark, fame linked to Indonesia's political pride
Located by the Hotel Indonesia Roundabout, which takes its name from the hotel

w: Opened in 1954, this military cemetery holds more than 7,000 casualties and veterans of the war of independence - including, oddly, Imperial Japanese soldiers who stayed on after 1945 to fight for Indonesian freedom. B.J. Habibie remains the only Indonesian president buried here; five vice presidents lie alongside him.
s: Where presidents, vice presidents and 7,000 veterans rest
_facts: Built 1953, opened 10 November 1954, in Kalibata, South Jakarta
More than 7,000 military casualties and veterans of Indonesian War of Independence buried, including Imperial Japanese Army veterans who stayed to fight for independence
B.J. Habibie is the only Indonesian president buried here (died 2019)
Five vice presidents buried there, from Adam Malik (1984) to Try Sutrisno (2026)

w: Housed in former Dutch East India Company warehouses by the old Sunda Kelapa harbour, this museum tracks Indonesia's maritime history through model fishing boats and the pinisi schooners still sailed by Bugis sailors today. A 2018 fire tore through much of it, though the collection was evacuated first.
s: Dutch trading warehouses turned maritime archive
_facts: Museum Bahari, located in old Sunda Kelapa harbour area, Penjaringan
Inaugurated inside former Dutch East India Company warehouses
Focuses on maritime history of Indonesia; displays fishing boat models and Bugis pinisi schooners
Much of museum destroyed by fire in January 2018; goods evacuated

w: Dutch colonial engineers dammed this valley in 1933 to create an artificial lake; on 27 March 2009 the 16-metre dam failed, draining the reservoir in a flood that killed at least 100 people in the town below. The lake remains, rebuilt - its 1933 concrete a reminder of how fast still water can turn violent.
s: A Dutch-built dam that broke and took a neighbourhood
_facts: Artificial lake near Cirendeu, South Tangerang
Formed by a dam up to 16m high built by Dutch colonial authorities in 1933
Dam failed 27 March 2009, draining the lake
Resulting floods killed at least 100 people

w: Facing Fatahillah Square alongside the Jakarta History Museum, this Kota Tua museum is devoted entirely to wayang - Javanese puppetry - tracing a tradition that's carried Javanese storytelling for centuries. One stop on a square that packs several heritage museums within a few footsteps of each other.
s: A whole museum for Java's shadow puppets
_facts: Museum Wayang, dedicated to Javan wayang puppetry
Located in Kota Tua, Jakarta
Faces Fatahillah Square, alongside Jakarta History Museum, Fine Art and Ceramic Museum

w: Completed in 1650 in the Chinatown quarter of Glodok, Vihara Dharma Bhakti - better known as Kim Tek Ie - holds the title of Jakarta's oldest Chinese temple. Nearly four centuries of continuous worship in one klenteng, tucked into streets that have changed around it many times over.
_facts: Also called Vihara Dharma Bhakti; a klenteng (Chinese temple)
Located in the Chinatown neighbourhood of Glodok, Jakarta
Completed in 1650
Oldest Chinese temple in Jakarta

w: Traced to a modest 1676 chapel for Batavia's Mardijker Christians, this church was rebuilt in permanent form by the Dutch East India Company between 1693 and 1695 and has barely changed since. Renamed Gereja Sion after independence, it may be Asia's oldest active Protestant church - colonial gravestones still inside.
s: Asia's oldest church still doing its original job
_facts: Historic Protestant church in Pinangsia, Taman Sari, Jakarta, dating to late 17th century
Roots traced to 1676 chapel for Mardijker people, serving Portuguese-language congregation
Rebuilt permanently by Dutch East India Company 1693-1695
Officially renamed GPIB Jemaat Sion / Gereja Sion in 1957
Possibly oldest continuously functioning Protestant church in Asia; holds colonial furniture, memorial boards, gravestones

w: Opened in 2009 inside the first headquarters of the Netherlands Indies gulden - the Dutch East Indies' central bank - this museum traces the currency's path to becoming Bank Indonesia after independence in 1953. A heritage building in Jakarta's Old Town, doing time as a monument to its own former job.
s: A Dutch-era bank vault turned money museum
_facts: Bank museum in Jakarta, founded by and named after Bank Indonesia
Opened 21 July 2009
Housed in heritage building that was first HQ of the Netherlands Indies gulden (De Javasche Bank), central bank of Dutch East Indies
Bank nationalized as Bank Indonesia in 1953 after independence
Located next to Mandiri Museum in Jakarta Old Town
